name: deepV12
description: 12 m offshore deep-V speedboat: the ONE set of defining numbers for the physics proxy (src/speedboat/hullMesh.ts) and the render hull (Blender). Physics builds its mesh from `spec`; `stations` is the generator's output at the proxy's own stations, pinned equal by tests/hullWater.test.ts.
frame: hull frame: x across the beam (symmetric, +x one side), y up from the keel baseline, z forward from the transom (z = 0 at the transom, z = loa at the stem)

scaling.law: mass, LCG, VCG and inertia DERIVED from `massItems` (deriveMassProperties); geometry set by concept sign-off: 12 m LOA, 24 deg deadrise, chine beam 2.30 m; hull depth keel to sheer 1.30 m at the transom (T179 part 3, was 1.674 m: see `derived.depthSource`)
scaling.check: overall beam with 8 deg flare over the top 0.60 m of topside = 2.47 m (flare knuckle 0.19 m above the chine: at the stem the chine is only 0.31 m under the 1.30 m deck, and the render blends the knuckle 0.3·(deck − chine) above it, which must stay under the deck edge), inside the 2.44-2.51 m of real 12 m deep-Vs (Cigarette 38 Top Gun: 11.43 m, 2.44 m beam, 24 deg, 4.49 t dry with twin sterndrives)

propPoint.note: centreline EQUIVALENT of the three drives (physics thrust point); per-engine points in `engines`

derived.sides: vertical from chine to deck in the physics proxy (flare is render-only)
derived.stem: forefoot at z = 11.65 (keel length), deck-level stem at z = 12: rake 0.35 m, modelled in the proxy (STYLE-SPEC C4). Plan: the chine half-beam tapers as cos from 60 % of the keel length to `spec.stemHalfBeamFraction` x 1.15 m = 6 mm at the stem (pointed bow, STYLE-SPEC silhouette rule 4; was a 0.04 floor = 9 cm wide nose). The sheer is CONSTANT (deckY 1.30 m): the upturn seen from below is the keel rise (bowKeelRise 0.982 m over the forward 30 %), not sheer
derived.deadrise: 24 deg constant aft of z 7.2 m (60% LOA), warping (t^2) to 45 deg at the forefoot; per-station values in `stations[].deadriseDeg` (STYLE-SPEC C8). Sources: Sport Fishing Mag "Perfect Boat Hull Designs" (Regulator 24 deg transom to 48-49 deg forward); Ray Hunt Design deep-V Q&A (deadrise varies continuously). Savitsky uses the TRANSOM (constant, prismatic) deadrise: 24 deg
derived.depthSource: Hull depth keel to sheer 1.30 m at the transom, freeboard chine to sheer 0.79 m. Measured off the 42 ft Apache Renegade 3-view (REFERENCES a1, drawing by Mark McManus Inc. 2015, 12.87 m LOA = 710 px): keel to rub rail 69-74 px = 1.25-1.34 m near the transom, keel to deck edge 83 px = 1.50 m, chine to rub rail about 0.9 m; lower bound APBA 2026 Offshore Rulebook Super Vee: >= 48 in (1.22 m) keel to deck ahead of the canopy (REFERENCES a15). No manufacturer publishes a hull depth for these boats (searched Cigarette, Fountain, Donzi specs). The old 1.674 m (chine 0.512 + freeboard 1.162) read as a workboat in the render. Deck-referenced mass items (roll arch, seat, pilot) moved down with the deck by 0.374 m; the FRP shell centroid scaled with the area-weighted section centroid (0.985 -> 0.792 m) and its own roll gyradius 0.966 -> 0.905 m (shorter topsides), mass unchanged (ASSUMED)

engines.model: Mercury Racing 450R V8 (4.6 L), 689 lb dry — ethanol variant assumed same mass
engines.propNote: propeller disc 0.55 m aft of the mounting plane (under the aft third of the 0.86 m cowl — ASSUMED from the cowl proportions) and 0.22 m below the anti-ventilation plate; T196: shaft AT the keel line, plate 0.22 m above it (was 0.10), so the surface-piercing prop runs part-surfaced in the transom wake hollow at speed (hullWater transomWake; immersion 0.6-0.7 at C_v 4-8, Kim & Rhee 2024 range 0.3-0.7) and buried at rest; outboard mass items raised with it. Previous basis for 0.10 m: planing boats run the plate flush to 1/2 in above the bottom, a bracketed outboard ~2 in higher because the prop runs in the hump behind the hull (TwoMorrow Holdings/Boat Builder Central, 'Outboard shaft lengths and transoms', 2016); setback rules of thumb give +1 in per 4–10 in of setback (+3 to +7.5 in at 30 in; boating forums). The prop disc spans the keel line: partly surface-piercing at speed, as Mercury Racing's Sport Master gearcase is designed to run

lowerUnit.note: Steering gearcase of each outboard as a low-aspect-ratio lateral foil (physics only; per-engine position from `engines[].mountX` / `mountZFromTransom`). ALL NUMBERS ASSUMED from the 30 in bracket and the prop point above: no gearcase drawing. Mercury Racing publish a 5.44 in (0.138 m) HD offshore torpedo; strut chord and skeg depth are typical-looking, not measured.
lowerUnit.steerAxisNote: the drive yaws about a vertical axis through the mount point (mountX, mountZFromTransom); steer + rotates the thrust line from body +z toward body +x
lowerUnit.profileDragNote: T189: was 0.02 (ASSUMED). Now from Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag (1965) ch. 6 streamlined strut C_D = 2C_f(1 + 2t/c + 60(t/c)^4) and body of revolution C_D,wet = C_f(1 + 1.5(d/l)^1.5 + 7(d/l)^3), C_f ITTC-57 at Re ~2e7 (0.0027), area-weighted over the strut 0.066 m2 (t/c 0.12), torpedo 0.076 m2 planform (d/l 0.25, wetted pi*d*l) and skeg 0.045 m2: 0.0086 on the 0.19 m2 lateral area. Free-surface spray drag of the piercing strut not included
lowerUnit.trimNote: T189: the lower unit trims about the clamp-bracket pin, at the top of the 30 in shaft above the AV plate (ASSUMED: pin at the clamp line). Range -6..+20 deg as given in the T189 task text for the 450R; NOT verified against a Mercury spec sheet (mercurymarine.com returned 403, no web budget left). propHand per engine: outer pair counter-rotating (port LH), centre RH - ASSUMED rigging
lowerUnit.areaNote: strut 0.22 m (plate to prop shaft) x 0.30 m chord + torpedo 0.55 m x 0.138 m (5.44 in HD offshore) + skeg 0.25 m x 0.18 m = 0.19 m2; span plate to skeg tip 0.50 m, geometric AR = 0.50^2/0.19 = 1.3; centre of area 0.21 m below the plate, mid-gearcase 0.35 m aft of the mount. ASSUMED proportions (no drawing)
lowerUnit.shaftNote: 450R shaft lengths 20/25/30 in (Boating Mag 450R review); shaft length = clamp to anti-ventilation plate (TwoMorrow Holdings 2016); 30 in XXL on the bracket

renderOnly.note: Features below the physics proxy's resolution. The proxy does NOT model them; values are ASSUMED typical, not from a drawing.
renderOnly.strakesPhysics: NOT in the physics proxy (5 cm flats are far below its 286-triangle resolution). Implication: real strakes stop the spray root at the first dry strake, so the Wagner splash-up width the proxy uses for the spray-root wetted area (friction) and for the 2D+t c may run wider than the real boat once c passes a strake; a strake-capped c is the proxy-side change if friction or lift reads high
